description: Sexual assaults on children often go unreported until the statute of limitations has expired. Civil litigation is one way to hold abusers accountable.
shortAnswer: Reporting sex abuse to the police does not always result in justice for your child. Sometimes civil litigation against a sex offender is an additional way to punish and deter the abuser from harming more children and to recover money to pay for the help you and your child need.

faq.q: Why does child sexual abuse often go unreported for so long?
faq.a: Pedophiles and pederasts are masters of manipulation and sometimes the child does not even know that what has happened to them is wrong. Perpetrators usually enjoy a position of trust and authority and use their position to hide the evidence of their wrongdoing, trying to shroud their sins until it is too late for the parents to take legal action.

faq.q: Where does child sexual abuse by people in positions of trust take place?
faq.a: Examples of settings within which such abuse takes place: churches, schools, sports teams, doctors/hospitals, Boy Scouts/Girl Scouts, day care centers, and homes (relatives sexually abusing children).

faq.q: What can a civil claim against a child's abuser pay for?
faq.a: A legal claim may provide much needed compensation to pay for medical treatment and counseling for you and your child.
